title: Distinct Arrangements After One Reversal
statement:
There are `N` balls of integral sizes, arranged in a line. The size of every ball lies between `X` and `Y` (both included). Two arrangements are considered different if some position holds balls of different sizes in the two arrangements.

You may perform the following operation **at most once**: choose two indices `a` and `b` with `1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ N` and reverse the order of all balls from position `a` to position `b`.

Count how many different arrangements you can end up with. The original arrangement counts too (perform no operation, or reverse a single ball).
input_format:
The first line contains three integers `N`, `X` and `Y`.
The second line contains `N` integers: the sizes of the balls from left to right.
output_format: Print one integer: the number of different arrangements that can be obtained.
constraints: X ≤ size of every ball ≤ Y

examples.explanation: All sizes are distinct, so every one of the 6 reversals with a < b gives a new arrangement, and none equals the original. With the original arrangement itself, that is 7.

Reversing a block whose two end balls have the same size gives the same result as reversing the block with those two ends removed, so only pairs of positions holding different sizes give new arrangements. There are 6 such pairs, plus the original arrangement.
Every reversal leaves the line unchanged, so only one arrangement exists.

hints: Brute force over all (a, b) pairs and put each result in a set to see the pattern on small inputs. Which pairs can never produce anything new?
If the balls at positions a and b have the same size, reversing [a, b] gives exactly the same line as reversing [a + 1, b - 1]. So you can always shrink a reversal until its two end balls differ.

After shrinking, a reversal with differing end sizes changes exactly positions a and b as its first and last difference from the original, so distinct pairs (a, b) give distinct arrangements. Count pairs with different sizes using a frequency table.
reference:
import sys
from collections import Counter

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = data[3:3 + n]
    cnt = Counter(a)
    total = n * (n - 1) // 2
    for c in cnt.values():
        total -= c * (c - 1) // 2
    print(total + 1)

main()
